*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

*Cittasaṁsaṭṭhaduka, Kusalattika* (Patthana 15.42) is an Abhidhamma treatise forming part of the canonical *Paṭṭhāna* collection. The text analyzes the conditional relations (*paccaya*) governing phenomena classified according to the matrix of the dyad on states conjoined with consciousness (*cittasaṁsaṭṭhaduka*) combined with the primary triad on wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate states (*kusalattika*).

No external cross-language parallels in Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan corpora are attested for this section [DharmaNexus]. Automated textual analysis by DharmaNexus identifies substantial internal text reuse within the Pali Abhidhamma, recording 51 shared passages across 21 other Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. Its most extensive textual overlaps are with adjacent and formally analogous combinatorial sections of the *Paṭṭhāna*, particularly *Mahantaraduka, Kusalattika* (Patthana 3.10), *Cittasamuṭṭhānaduka, Kusalattika* (Patthana 15.43), *Sārammaṇaduka, Kusalattika* (Patthana 15.38), and other consciousness-related dyads including *Cittasaṁsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhānaduka* (Patthana 15.46) and *Cittasahabhūduka* (Patthana 15.44) [DharmaNexus].
